Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Health-related anxiety
- Patient Goal(s): Gain reassurance and strategies to control worry about serious illness; reduce health-related internet searching
- Clinical Goal(s): Decrease health anxiety symptoms; improve coping with uncertainty; prevent maladaptive reassurance-seeking
- Actions (Patient):
  • Maintain headache diary (triggers, symptoms, management)  
  • Limit online symptom searching to reputable sites agreed with clinician  
  • Practice scheduled worry time and relaxation techniques (to be taught)  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide psychoeducation on health anxiety and migraine vs. red-flag symptoms  
  • Teach basic CBT-informed strategies or refer for structured CBT if worries persist  
  • Review in 1 week to assess anxiety level and headache frequency  

Secondary Problem: Work-related stress
- Patient Goal(s): Manage workplace pressure without excessive sick leave
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce stress impact on physical and mental health; encourage healthy lifestyle
- Actions (Patient):
  • Identify and schedule at least two stress-reducing activities weekly (e.g., light exercise, mindfulness)  
  • Discuss manageable workload adjustments with manager if needed  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide brief counselling on stress management techniques  
  • Offer certificate or workplace letter if clinically indicated  
  • Monitor for emerging mood symptoms at follow-up  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Difference between migraine and brain tumor; health anxiety; headache diary; medication use
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Escalating frequency/intensity of worry, persistent googling, functional impairment, new neurological deficits
- Coping Strategies: Relaxation breathing, scheduled problem-solving, limiting unhelpful online searches, regular exercise, maintaining sleep hygiene

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (verbal)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Yes
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently; CBT referral to be considered
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: 1 week or sooner if symptoms escalate

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Migraine with visual aura – High: DDx cites classic unilateral throbbing pain, visual aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting, family history.
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – Medium: DDx notes new severe headache, positional worsening, recent estrogen OCP use; no neuro deficits.
- Intracranial mass/brain tumor – Low: DDx notes positional headache and vomiting but lacks progressive course or focal signs.
